A stalwart priced like this usually makes me want to buy more, but a P/E of 7 on an insurer makes me ask whether I'm looking at peak earnings, because catastrophe years and the pricing cycle can crush profits quickly. I could not check the 3-year growth trend, insider buying, institutional ownership, free cash flow or margin trend, because they are not in this snapshot, and missing checks do not count as passed. I am not putting a fair-value number on it, because the data in front of me doesn't support one, so margin of safety is shown as zero. I hold, I don't trim a winner whose story is intact, and I won't add until the gaps are filled. My stalwart rule says sell after a 30-50% gain in one to two years, and at 18% we are not there yet.

rationale: I own 14 shares, bought at $24.37 and now $24.34, so the position is basically flat after 85 days, and the question is whether to keep it. On the numbers I can see, this is a Fast Grower: 48.3% growth, a P/E of 19.95 and a PEG of 0.41, which is cheap for the growth. Debt-to-equity of 0.46 passes my test. But growth near 50% makes me cautious, the five-year and three-year rates are identical, and I could not check insider activity, institutional ownership, free cash flow or margins because the snapshot does not report them. I have not done an intrinsic value calculation here, so I set it equal to the price and show no margin of safety. I hold, I don't add until those gaps are closed, and I sell if the story breaks, not because the price wiggled.

rationale: I own two shares at a $140.01 entry, up 7.14%, and I'm keeping them. The reported numbers look like a Fast Grower: a PEG of 0.417 and debt-to-equity of just 0.012. But five-year growth of 103% is above the 50% level where I start doubting sustainability, so I won't trust that PEG at face value. Insider activity, institutional ownership, free cash flow, margins and earnings consistency are not reported in this snapshot, so I can't confirm those criteria and I won't add to the position on the numbers I have. rationale: I own this one, and it's up about 47% since May, so the question is whether to keep it, not whether to open it. On the numbers I have, it's a Fast Grower: 51.35% five-year earnings growth against a 25.17 P/E gives a PEG of 0.49. As I always say, a fairly priced company has a P/E equal to its growth rate, and this one sits far below that. But growth above 50% makes me nervous about sustainability. The snapshot says nothing about the business itself, insider buying, institutional ownership, margins or cash flow. Missing data lowers my confidence, so I keep the position as is, I don't add, and I don't cut a winner just because it has gone up. I sell only if the story breaks.
